object_description: elongated flat two-storey structure with a vertically lamellar facade
design_condition: the long flat body runs along the street, adopts the eaves height of the neighbouring building and uses the entire available above-ground area, reducing the surrounding space to a minimum

positive: Adopting the eaves height of the existing building gives an appropriate two-storey appearance towards the street
Using the entire available footprint is acceptable in view of the situation and the use of these outdoor spaces
The presence of the building is enhanced by a strong, vertically lamellar structure
The street becomes a shared square in the area of the main entrances
A generous covered entrance provides precise access that is easy for everyone to find
The break hall is well designed in itself
A courtyard illuminates the interior offices in the north-eastern area
The restriction to two storeys is advantageous for use, with hardly any floors to climb
Very small floor areas and a small building volume compared to the other projects
The project makes a significant contribution and has interesting urban and architectural qualities
negative: Cutting the upper school path into the terrain detracts from the otherwise confident handling of the topography
The cut severely separates the break hall from the elementary school playground
The garage entrance increases traffic and impairs the use of the entrance square
The spiral staircase obstructs the hall and restricts its use, and its form appears somewhat sought-after
The circumferential corridor is sparsely lit with natural light on the ground floor
A statement on the structural concept inside the building is missing
Overhang, heavy concrete rod facade and the round stair cut-out give a structurally unfavourable situation with high costs
The facade is elaborately constructed and the added value of its forced expression is questionable
The topography is ignored due to the lack of a plinth
The architectural expression appears somewhat alien in the context
Some rooms are too small compared to the programme, with hardly any room for manoeuvre
The combination of dining area, smoking area and bicycle rack access is not convincing
Courtyard-facing offices will not be as popular as rooms with a view out, and some meeting rooms have little daylight
Almost square classrooms are difficult to use
Form factor and building construction result in rather mediocre cost efficiency
